title: Bridges and tunnels: information for insurance assessment

seo.title: Bridge and tunnel insurance assessment in Moldova | ING Broker
seo.description: Prepare site information, methods, studies, participants and schedules. Separate new works, existing property and liability without assuming completion guarantees.
seo.keywords: bridge insurance Moldova, tunnel insurance, infrastructure project insurance, existing structures, construction risk assessment

author: ING Broker editorial team
content:
Assessing bridge or tunnel insurance requires information about the works and their environment. Contract value alone does not describe the risk. For a project in Moldova, prepare technical records, schedules and participants' insurance obligations separately.

Separate the new structure from existing property

For rehabilitation, identify existing, demolished and reconstructed sections. For a new tunnel, describe surroundings, available investigations and construction method. This is a technical brief, not a substitute for engineering expertise or a geotechnical study.

  • Available geotechnical and relevant hydrological studies.
  • Construction method, temporary works and monitoring.
  • Neighbouring buildings, infrastructure and utilities.
  • Contractors, designers and subcontractors with their roles.
  • Testing, acceptance and opening for use.

Consider a hypothetical infrastructure project whose sequence changes for one section. Summarise differences from the earlier schedule, replaced documents and actual status, marking pending answers. A preliminary decision is not an approved final method merely because its price effect appears small.

Questions about proposed conditions

Ask about water ingress, ground conditions, design defects and reinstatement costs without treating them as implicitly covered. Discuss material damage, third-party claims and delay consequences separately. Clarify potential inspection and technical-change notification requirements.

Versioned documents for designers and insurance assessment

Keep a list of plans and studies with dates and versions. If methods change, identify replaced documents and reasons. Do not mix preliminary studies and final reports without explanation. Assessors need the basis of the description, and project teams should be able to locate the same records.

For missing information, record who can confirm it and which document is expected. Avoid approximate answers about ground, existing assets or surroundings merely to close a form. An open point can be assessed honestly; an assumption presented as fact can distort comparison. This is organisation guidance, not universal contractual duty or technical approval.

Describe the risk through works and location

A new bridge, rehabilitation and a tunnel in a built-up area cannot be assessed only by contract value. Prepare a description of the structure, construction method and surrounding environment. Use the documentation for the Moldovan site concerned. An online project of similar dimensions does not confirm your work is eligible.

Separate what is built, already exists and is temporary. A support structure, rented machine and neighbouring network have different roles. Do not assume one amount includes all. Ask for each item to be identified in the property being assessed and in the proposed conditions.

Designers confirm their documentation and project management its dates, while contractual obligations require competent review. Do not ask an administrator to certify ground conditions, strength or liability. For temporary works, check composition, owner and period without automatically inferring changed insured values or acceptance.

What a useful technical presentation contains

Show project stage and available records. Explain which studies or calculations are still being updated and what remains unconfirmed. A preliminary sketch is not a final design. Clear versions prevent confusion from near-identical file names and allow missing information to be requested.

  • Customer, principal contractor and main participants.
  • Location, dimensions and structural function.
  • Method and important stages.
  • Available geotechnical, hydrological and other investigations.
  • Temporary works, machinery and existing elements.
  • Surroundings, utilities and planned monitoring.
  • Testing, acceptance and opening schedule.

This is preparation, not a universal requirement or technical opinion. Final information depends on assessment. Do not publish detailed plans or confidential records through an article form. Agree the channel and authorised recipients before sending the complete file.

Identify the original condition before rehabilitation

Record documents describing existing condition and planned interventions. Separate known deterioration from potential future damage. Discovery during works does not prove the problem originated then. Preserve technical reports without altering conclusions to fit presumed insurance conditions.

Ask about existing property being worked on and assets merely nearby. Request definitions and limits of any named category. Acceptance of new works' value does not establish cover for the entire bridge. The insurer assesses the presented configuration; the broker does not certify structural strength.

For existing structures, identify which records describe condition and the works concerned. An administrator can confirm a report exists but cannot infer technical suitability from its title. Refer unclear matters to competent specialists and keep pending information open. Do not substitute an approximate description borrowed from a familiar project.

Discuss ground, water and surroundings using evidence

For work near water or unusual ground, provide investigations and design assumptions. Ask what further information is needed and how unforeseen conditions are treated. “All risks” does not eliminate exclusions or site-related conditions.

For tunnels or work near buildings and utilities, record known surroundings and professionally planned monitoring. Do not estimate settlement, pressure or safe levels from this article. It helps organise insurance questions. It does not select a construction method or assess worksite safety.

Check all parties use the same design version. A proposal for an earlier method and a newly titled certificate may look consistent without explaining their relationship. Preserve dates and changed schedules. Do not edit insurer documents yourself; request clarification for the actual configuration and stage.

Do not omit temporary works

A platform, scaffold or temporary structure may have separate value and ownership. State whether made for the project, rented or used elsewhere. Separate its construction cost from machinery placed on it. Ask how each item is valued and when possible protection starts or ends.

Method changes can alter this list without substantially changing contract price. Summarise differences and request declaration procedures. Acceptance of one project version does not accept every subsequent technical solution. Final records should relate to actual execution.

Use a working table with the customer's exact question, the response in the received version and the supporting document. Do not reduce a broad clause to “fulfilled”. Where it combines property, liability and timing, separate the questions without pretending that this changes the contract or establishes acceptance of every component.

Check subcontractor and designer roles separately

Prepare one list of the participants and the activities each performs. Match named insureds to obligations and existing policies. A subcontractor in a schedule is not automatically insured. Designer professional liability is not the same as material damage insurance for the works.

Where a customer requests certificates or limits, keep the exact requirement and compare complete records. Do not add certificate wording unsupported by the policy. Obtain competent Moldovan review of contracts and legal responsibilities. Insurance assessment does not replace it.

If a customer wants an updated certificate, compare the request with the complete policy. Do not insert convenient unsupported wording. Keep versions and answers traceable without publishing confidential plans. This hypothetical example is not an ING Broker customer, engineering recommendation or completion guarantee.

Testing and opening are important milestones

Identify planned tests, responsible people and when others may use the structure. Do not confuse testing with normal operation. Ask for contractual stage boundaries. For partial opening, identify the section and date rather than assigning one status to the whole project.

Retain test reports and the relevant acceptance records. Delayed acceptance and material damage are different. Ask separately about financial consequences without assuming guaranteed deadlines or revenue. Additional solution availability and conditions require actual confirmation.

Example: equal values, different property

In an illustrative comparison, proposals have the same total. One describes new works only, while another includes certain existing assets with a separate limit. Equal totals do not make them equivalent. Compare definitions, limits and exclusions using the same list of property and works. This is not a real offer or product recommendation.

Check the deductible, meaning the portion retained under the contract, for each category. Ask about investigation, salvage or reinstatement costs and conditions. Record differences. An empty field is not acceptance, and a verbal answer does not replace final wording.

Incidents and restarting works

If a dangerous situation arises, follow the technical and emergency procedures with the appropriate specialist assistance. Do not enter an unsafe area for documentation. Preserve chronology, affected area, project stage and available records only where safely obtainable.

Separate urgent measures from permanent reinstatement and request contractual notification and inspection procedures. Do not promise on the insurer's behalf that expenses will be accepted. Restart decisions belong to competent technical people; broker discussion is not safety approval. Keep technical documents and insurance correspondence separate, while retaining references that allow the records to be matched by event and date.

Frequently asked questions for complex projects

Are all subcontracted works included?

Check insured parties, declared activities and applicable clauses. Site presence alone does not confirm protection.

Can I use a previous project's proposal?

Only as a question list. New sites, methods and contracts need separate assessment.

Does insurance guarantee completion on time?

No. Project management, contractual guarantees and possible financial coverage are different assessments.

Next step

Request a discussion with ING Broker to check assessment and brokering possibilities. The broker explains options and acts as intermediary. Risk acceptance, conditions and claims decisions belong to the insurer under the contract. This guide does not confirm product availability or cover for an individual case.
